blocks.content:
A Constitutional Amendment refers to a change or modification in the Constitution to adapt to changing political, social, and economic conditions.
Important Points:
• Parliament has the power to amend the Constitution.
• Some amendments require a special majority.
• Certain amendments also require approval from half of the State Legislatures.
A Constitutional Amendment refers to a change or modification in the Constitution to adapt to changing political, social, and economic conditions.

items: Parliament holds the power to amend the Constitution, a frequent question in polity exams.
Pay attention to the dual requirement for federal amendments: Special Majority in Parliament + Approval from at least half of the State Legislatures.

blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: A Constitutional Amendment modifies the Constitution to adapt to evolving political, social, and economic conditions.
The power to amend the Constitution is vested in the Parliament.
Certain amendments require a special majority, while specific ones additionally require approval from half of the State Legislatures.
